extraction.Name: Lena Brown Bull—nee Glenn
extraction.Tribe/Reservation: Shannon County, South Dakota (Pine Ridge area)
extraction.Refused/Protested: did not want her patent to her 160 acre allotment at the time it was issued, on account of not wanting to pay taxes, but she was informed by the Indian Agency that it was reported to the tax collector; that she would either have the taxes to pay, or that it would be sold for taxes after so long a time; so she accepted it
extraction.Sold/Mortgaged: sold her allotment, in 1920, for $900.00 cash
extraction.Buyer: John Short, of Potato Creek, South Dakota, for $900.00 cash
extraction.Tax burden forced sale/Mortgage: she thinks he paid the taxes for this one year she held her patent in fee
extraction.Occupation/Income: both he and she work what they can for a neighboring farmer, and this is the only source of income they have
extraction.NOTES: Mentally competent, has good health except that she has rheumatism; has three children to support, and they have good health; husband has poor health as he has tuberculosis and cannot work much; deponent also receives a monthly ration from the United States Government; document subscribed November 24, 1928
